angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 769,444 km at 9.13 pc = 1.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 109.53 +/- 0.17 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 9.13 +/- 0.014 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 108.7250 +/- 0.1645 mas (same row, RUWE 2.46), 661.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.106 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.127 +/- 0.011 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.106 +/- 0.011 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 769,444 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.045 +/- 0.013 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.045 +/- 0.013 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5936 +/- 33 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5936 +/- 33 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5936 +/- 33 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/beta-comae-berenices.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.370, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 114710) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
